summary.intent: Analyze 350-trace Neatlogs analytics dashboard screenshots and ship VeriFix v3 Coalesced Graph-Brain Turbo with single-pass coalesced planning and patching, content-addressed caching, a fast test runner, and a fully passing test suite.
summary.outcome: VeriFix v3 Coalesced Graph-Brain Turbo (exp_bd53a0e4a4) was shipped with -94.27% prompt tokens, -92.87% total tokens, -88.68% latency, -94.92% modeled enterprise COGS/run, 2.7ms warm cache, 36.8ms fast -S test runner, and 17/17 pytest passing in 39.49s across 21 modified files.

repo: Project uses a multi-layer architecture: agent_harness, graph_engine, entire_intelligence, aws_verifier, and neatlogs_mcp_client as distinct modules under src/verifix/
Benchmarks are tracked in a verified_runs_ledger.json and a CFO-oriented cfo_ai_verified_model.json, indicating a strong emphasis on cost modeling and auditability
Documentation includes both a docs/index.html and hackathon.md, suggesting the project targets both production and hackathon/demo audiences

Screenshots of Neatlogs analytics (350 traces, 21 tools, error/detection mix, orphan audit) are versioned directly in docs/screenshots/, implying observability artifacts are treated as first-class project assets
A plan.xlsx and BUSINESS_PLAN.md coexist, indicating business justification is maintained alongside technical artifacts

code.finding: EntireGraphEngine implements content-addressed caching achieving 2.7ms warm cache hit latency; caching is keyed on graph/Lambda content identity
Central harness was the primary edit target for the v3 coalesced single-pass planning and patching logic, consolidating what were previously multi-pass prompt flows
Implements a fast -S (no-capture) test runner mode achieving 36.8ms execution, distinct from the full 39.49s pytest suite
Houses the 17-test pytest suite that validates the v3 release; all 17/17 pass, serving as the release gate
Likely encapsulates the coalesced Graph-Brain Turbo intelligence layer; modified as part of the single-pass coalescing refactor
Script generates the CFO AI cost workbook (plan.xlsx / cfo_ai_verified_model.json), automating financial modeling from benchmark run data

workflow: Neatlogs MCP client is used for trace-level observability, with 350 traces analyzed across 21 tools to validate performance claims before shipping
Experiment IDs (e.g., exp_bd53a0e4a4) are embedded in commit/release metadata, enabling reproducible benchmark attribution
Token and latency reductions are validated against a modeled enterprise COGS metric, bridging engineering metrics to business impact
Screenshots of analytics dashboards are captured and versioned as part of the release artifact set, not just kept in external tools
